intent: Customer wants to know why she got an unpaid Direct Debit letter for her £750 rent to Northgate Lettings and a text from the agency asking for a manual payment, when £750 went out on 21 Sep. She wants to avoid both arrears and paying twice.
summary: Answer now from the bank's records instead of checking the mandate again. The 18 Sep collection was returned unpaid because funds were short; the 19 Sep letter is about that attempt. On 21 Sep Northgate collected again and the £750 was paid. So the bank shows September's £750 has left her account once, and nothing more is due before 18 Oct. Tell her the bank can't confirm Northgate's own records or arrears status. Before she pays manually, she should contact Northgate using details she already trusts, quoting the 21 Sep payment.

facts.claim: On 18 Sep the £750 Direct Debit to H&V COLLECT / NORTHGATE LETTINGS was returned unpaid ('refer to payer'). The available balance was £710.40.

The bank's automated letter dated 19 September 2026 says the £750 Direct Debit presented on 18 September could not be paid. It says no fee was charged and that the organisation may try to collect again.
A £2,145.00 salary was credited on 20 Sep.
On 21 Sep the originator collected the £750 again and it was paid, leaving a balance of £2,105.40. The payment carries reference NL-9LIME-0442.
H&V charged no unpaid-item fee. No further collection is scheduled before 18 Oct.

A machine OCR of the screenshot shows a text from 'Northgate Lettings' timestamped Tue 22 Sep, 16:20. It says the September Direct Debit failed and asks for a manual £750 payment that day to 'our client account', reference NL-9LIME-0442. The original image could not be read directly.
The customer does not want to be in arrears or to pay twice.
The agent told the customer they would check both dates on the mandate.

missing: Whether Northgate Lettings' own ledger has recorded the 21 Sep re-presented payment, and whether it shows any arrears. Only Northgate can confirm this; the customer should ask them directly.
Whether the 22 Sep text came from Northgate. The original image is unread and only an OCR transcription is available.

steps.instruction: Reply in the current chat: 'Thanks for waiting, Ms Patel. I've checked both dates. On 18 September Northgate Lettings tried to collect £750 by Direct Debit, but only £710.40 was available, so it was returned unpaid. That's what our letter of 19 September was about, and we didn't charge you a fee. Your salary arrived on 20 September, and on 21 September Northgate collected the £750 again. That payment went through and is on your statement with reference NL-9LIME-0442. So our records show September's £750 rent has been paid once. If you also make the manual £750 payment, Northgate would have £1,500 from you for September. Their text was sent on 22 September, the day after the payment, so their system may not have caught up yet. We can't see Northgate's own records or tell you whether they show you in arrears. Before you pay anything else, please contact Northgate using contact details you already have, such as your tenancy paperwork, and tell them the £750 was collected on 21 September with reference NL-9LIME-0442. If you're ever given new bank details for a payment by text, please check them with Northgate the same way first. There's no further collection from this Direct Debit scheduled before 18 October.'

rationale.explanation: The internal account view and the statement already show the 18 Sep return, the 19 Sep letter and the paid 21 Sep re-presentation, so they answer the customer's question without another mandate check. The agency's ledger and the source of the text are not shown in the evidence, so the reply sends her to Northgate through trusted contact details rather than declaring her paid up or the text fake.
rationale.criterion: Use the supplied mandate and collection records directly, and separate a returned collection from a later paid re-presentation. Bank records do not show whether the merchant has recorded the payment, so do not claim that.

must_state: The 18 Sep collection of £750 was returned unpaid because the available balance was £710.40. The 19 Sep letter is about that attempt.
On 21 Sep Northgate collected the £750 again and it was paid from her account. The bank's records show September's £750 has been paid once.
H&V charged no fee for the unpaid item, and no further collection is scheduled before 18 Oct.
If she also makes the manual £750 payment, she would have paid Northgate £1,500 for September.

The bank cannot confirm Northgate's own records or whether they show her in arrears. She should contact Northgate using contact details she already has (for example from her tenancy paperwork), not only by replying to the text, and quote the 21 Sep payment, reference NL-9LIME-0442.
The text was sent on 22 Sep, after the 21 Sep payment, so Northgate's system may not have been updated yet. This is a possible reason, not a confirmed one.
must_not: Do not say Northgate has received, matched or recorded the 21 Sep payment, or that she is definitely not in arrears.
Do not say the agency text is a scam or fraudulent. Do not say it is definitely genuine either.
Do not tell her to make the manual payment, and do not promise a refund if she pays twice.
Do not say the 21 Sep payment can be reversed or that a Direct Debit Guarantee claim applies.
Do not tell her the bank will re-check the mandate or come back later, because the dates are already established.
Do not ask for PINs, passwords or one-time codes.
